original_query: SELECT * FROM (SELECT DEPTNO FROM EMP WHERE DEPTNO < 4) AS t7 INNER JOIN (SELECT * FROM (SELECT DEPTNO FROM EMP WHERE DEPTNO > 7 UNION ALL SELECT DEPTNO FROM EMP) AS t11 WHERE DEPTNO < 4) AS t12 ON t7.DEPTNO = t12.DEPTNO
rewritten_query:
SELECT e1.DEPTNO, e2.DEPTNO
FROM EMP e1
JOIN EMP e2
  ON e1.DEPTNO = e2.DEPTNO
WHERE e1.DEPTNO < 4
  AND e2.DEPTNO < 4;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: The UNION ALL branch 'SELECT DEPTNO FROM EMP WHERE DEPTNO > 7' can never produce rows after the outer filter DEPTNO < 4 (mutually exclusive predicates), so it was removed entirely.
Nested derived tables (t7, t11, t12) were flattened: the inner UNION ALL with the outer DEPTNO < 4 filter reduces to simply EMP filtered by DEPTNO < 4, eliminating an extra full table scan.

The join of two derived tables over the same base table was rewritten as a direct self-join of EMP with the DEPTNO < 4 predicate pushed to both sides, preserving the multiset semantics (N² duplicate rows per deptno). A SELECT DISTINCT/collapse was avoided since it would break equivalence.

Applying DEPTNO < 4 on both join sides explicitly (redundant via equality but harmless) helps the optimizer push filters early and enables index usage on EMP(DEPTNO); consider an index on EMP(DEPTNO) given the selective filter against a 45M-row table.
